correctness.rationale: For each exponent the zero-sum quadratic form is exactly 2^p [t sum S_j² - sum alpha_u²]; Cauchy within each part reduces it to a diagonal k-part form, and equality conditions are exact. Repeated maximal parts give the r−1 radical. A unique maximal part gives a strictly monotone secular root and a one-dimensional explicit equality vector. Schoenberg and Taylor expansion establish iff all-scales kernel positivity. Double-centering yields exact endpoint Euclidean ranks. The sharp log2 3 gap is forced by induced isometric K3,1, K2,1,1 or K2,2 and strict part enlargement. Standard-library exact rational checker passed all 119 profiles of order ≤10, including 32 exact repeated-maximum rank checks, and verified K3,2,1 algebraic root. Finite tests are not used to infer the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: A parameter-free finite-metric test and a known two-part formula do not give a usable closed sharp phase diagram for all unequal multipartite sizes. The family is canonical, its negative-type threshold controls universal Gaussian-kernel admissibility and optimal Euclidean snowflake embedding, and the theorem identifies an arithmetically nontrivial secular boundary, all equality nullspaces, and the strongest possible gap below the exceptional P3. This is a complete natural infinite-family classification, not an isolated numerical slice; future use includes finite covariance/kernel design and metric embeddings.
